It doesn't really affect me emotionally, not when I consider my own death. I've meditated frequently and heavily for some time, and it seems to have helped me come to terms with mortality, my family and my own included. The one person who could die, and I would not be prepared for, is my sister. That thought does bother me a bit.

I've considered the experience of dying heavily, again through mediation, but also as a child. I was raised catholic, and you can't ignore death when your home is littered with graphic crucifixes, and pictures of heaven and hell. I still remember an artwork my grandmother owned. It depicted an infinite line of people approaching a fork in the road, and some walked up to heaven, and greet St. Peter, while some entered hell.

As a teen I really got into industrial music, and then metal, and then everything far and inbetween. From electrogoth, to death metal, the concept of death was part of my daily dose of music. One of the biggest names in metal is Death. One of Metallica's albums features tracks exclusively on different ways to die. One of Slayer's albums was inspired by their time in the middle east.

Maybe it was Catholicism and prayers that read, "If I die before I wake", maybe it was songs like, "Angel of Death", maybe it was meditation, but I don't really feel too much of an emotional response from the possibility of my death.
